intro: Sometimes feature coordinates are implicit and only inner products are available. Double centering removes the feature mean directly from a Gram matrix.
task: Center a square symmetric kernel matrix by subtracting its row and column means and restoring its grand mean.
requirements: kernel is a square matrix symmetric within absolute tolerance 1e-10. Positive semidefiniteness is not checked in this algebra exercise.
Center the supplied training kernel on both axes. Do not divide by a variance, subtract only the diagonal, or reuse this formula unchanged for an out-of-sample rectangular kernel.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: One observation

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Expand the inner product of two centered feature vectors to see the four terms needed in kernel space.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Subtract row and column means, then restore the grand mean because it was removed twice.

explanation: If K=X X.T, centering the feature rows first gives (X-mean(X))(X-mean(X)).T. Expanding that product yields the two mean subtractions and one grand-mean addition.
A centered training Gram matrix has row and column sums near zero. Adding a constant to every original kernel entry disappears under the transformation.
